expectations.text: Overall verdict is Low likelihood / does NOT read as AI-generated
expectations.evidence: Short answer up front: 'Does this read as generic or AI-generated? Short answer: No.' Bottom line restates: 'This does **not** read as AI-generated.'

expectations.text: Recognizes the committed editorial/print aesthetic as intentional (font pairing, sharp geometry, drop cap, marginalia, or colophon mentioned)
expectations.evidence: Section 3: 'A single committed concept, carried everywhere... a drop cap; a margin note keyed with ※; a colophon that names the typefaces.' Also notes 'Zero border-radius... Everything is sharp, square, print-like' and the Libre Caslon Text + IBM Plex Mono pairing as 'a *system*, not a random pairing.'

expectations.text: Does not flag the serif font or the deep-red accent as AI-slop false positives
expectations.evidence: The accent is defended, not flagged: '#a41f13, a deep oxblood/editorial red... meaningfully darker and cooler than the coral/terracotta family, and it belongs to a real print lineage (rubrication).' The serif is praised: 'Libre Caslon Text (a bookish, slightly sharp Caslon revival)... purposeful pairing.'

expectations.text: Does not recommend a wholesale redesign — only minor refinements
expectations.evidence: Section 4 frames all findings as minor: 'None of these undermine the design's distinctiveness; they are polish and accessibility items' (preconnect, skip link, touch targets, placeholder links, meta tags). No redesign suggested anywhere.

expectations.text: Uses a structured audit format with evidence for any findings
expectations.evidence: Structured sections (Verdict at a Glance table, item-by-item AI-slop checklist, What Is Working, Honest Gaps, Bottom Line) with concrete evidence: measured contrast ratios (17.98:1, 7.54:1), specific CSS values (clamp(4rem, 14vw, 10rem), --measure: 62ch, padding-block: 0.5rem).
